Palantir Stocks Edge Higher With Earnings Facing a Narrow Revenue Expectation Gap Less than 1 min read

PLTR Palantir PLTR faces a narrow revenue hurdle and a bigger test of what comes next. The enterprise and government AI software provider heads into its November 2 earnings report with expected revenue less than 1% above its guidance midpoint. Shares rose 0.77% to $185.53 at 9:32 a.m. ET on November 2. With that small gap, the outlook could carry more weight than a modest quarterly beat. The Stocktwits preview published by Yahoo Finance puts expected revenue at $2.18 billion, against company guidance of $2.160 billion$2.164 billion. Palantir's August results outlined adjusted operating income of $1.292 billion$1.296 billion and full-year adjusted free cash flow of $4.5 billion$4.7 billion. Its November 2 results webcast is scheduled for 5 p.m. ET. The revenue estimate sits roughly 0.8% above the guidance midpoint, while the operating-income midpoint implies an adjusted margin near 60%.

The sharper question: can Palantir sustain that margin and lift its cash-flow outlook? Those signals could tell investors more than a small revenue surprise. The GuruFocus graphic shows a GF Score of 85/100, with momentum and growth standing out while profitability trails the other dimensions. That profile adds another reason to watch whether expanding AI adoption translates into durable earnings and cash generation.

item.content:encoded:

Apple Stocks Move Lower With Earnings Facing a Distorted Margin Comparison Less than 1 min read

AAPL Apple AAPL heads into tonight's results with a margin hurdle investors should watch closely. Shares fell 1.15% to $340.68 at 9:40 a.m. ET on November 2. The consumer-device and services group's prior-quarter gross margin was 50.1%, but removing a disclosed tariff-refund benefit brings the comparison to roughly 48.1%. That lower baseline could give a clearer read on underlying profitability. Apple reported $109.4 billion in revenue in its July 30 release, with tariff refunds adding approximately two percentage points to gross margin. Reuters' November 2 earnings preview cites LSEG estimates of $113.39 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, including $31.56 billion from Services. Rising memory costs put margins in focus, while the holiday-quarter outlook could help investors judge whether demand can absorb that pressure.

Services would account for roughly 27.8% of revenue under those estimates, making the business a key test of Apple's ability to defend profitability as component costs climb. The GuruFocus snapshot shows a 95/100 GF Score, with profitability and growth standing out, but a price-to-earnings ratio of 39.06 suggests investors are already paying for strong performance. Tonight's report needs to show how underlying margins and the holiday outlook measure up to those expectations.
